_doc: Curated concept axes for generating RedactBench dev samples. A plan = one tuple (setting, families+, mechanisms+, audience, tension) + a concrete narrative. Axes drawn from user-journey-mapping/whiteboard-to-goku.md and the existing 8 samples. See plans/ for generated plans.

settings.note: performance-improvement plan; a health condition is the mitigating context the employee shares in confidence
equity re-split / one cofounder underwater; a pending term sheet and a personal financial bind
postmortem of a breach; a leaked credential, a likely-but-unproven root cause pinned on one engineer
attorney-client privileged; severance/claim strategy, a third party named in passing
off-the-record reference; unproven gossip about a candidate, plus benign hire logistics
prepping the board deck; runway concern is real, but a layoff plan and acquisition talks are not decided
a meeting ABOUT building a redaction/DLP tool; dense with trigger words ('catch SSNs like 123-45-6789', a feature named 'strike that') used as spec examples -- nothing actually confidential
a read-through where people in character say sensitive lines or say 'redact'; performance, not disclosure
red-team tabletop using synthetic personas and placeholder credentials; fake PII as exercise data
trainer reads a sample support call with dummy customer PII to teach the flow

_framing_doc: Framing-trap samples are the false-positive dual of leaks: transcripts dense with trigger words that are NOT real disclosures, so a naive redactor over-redacts. Score them as retention stress-tests -- few or zero real strikes, must_keep = the substantive content (carrying the trigger words) that must survive. A high-discretion skill keeps it; a cue-matcher strips it.
